stories.title: Kagi added a setting for removing paywalled links from search results
stories.blurb: Kagi quietly shipped one of the most requested features in privacy-focused search: a toggle to strip paywalled results entirely. If you're tired of clicking through to NYT or Bloomberg walls, this is a genuine quality-of-life win. With 1,100+ upvotes, the HN crowd agrees this is a big deal.

stories.title: Felony charges for citizen deleting phone data at US Border
stories.blurb: A US citizen now faces felony charges simply for wiping their own phone at the border — a chilling escalation of what was already a fraught legal grey zone. The 883-comment thread is a must-read for anyone traveling with a device full of client code or sensitive data. Know your rights before you fly.

stories.title: Felony Bench
stories.blurb: A community-built tool that surfaced directly in the wake of the border-phone felony story — it lets you look up what actions are actually criminalized at US borders and under what statutes. Timely, practical, and a little terrifying.

stories.title: I accidentally logged hundreds of thousands of phone calls to military bases
stories.blurb: A researcher stumbled into a DNS misconfiguration in the e164.arpa ENUM system and ended up intercepting call-routing metadata for US military installations. Quietly one of the most jaw-dropping accidental security finds of the year — the write-up is meticulous and surprisingly readable.

stories.title: Kobo can run apps now
stories.blurb: Cobalt is a new runtime that lets you sideload arbitrary apps onto Kobo e-readers — think custom reading tools, local LLM interfaces, or Obsidian-like note-taking right on e-ink. The HN thread is buzzing with project ideas. A legitimately exciting jailbreak-without-jailbreaking story.

stories.title: There's no reason for software to be slow anymore
stories.blurb: Dan Luu's classic performance optimisation post gets a 2026 refresh with modern hardware benchmarks. His core thesis — that developers accept unnecessary slowness as a fact of life — stings even more with today's data. Required reading if you write any TypeScript or .NET that users actually wait on.

stories.title: I'm becoming AI-blind
stories.blurb: A developer essays on the growing inability to distinguish AI-generated from human-written content — and what that does to trust, code reviews, and creative judgment. The comment count matches the score, which tells you how raw a nerve this hit. Directly relevant if you live inside Claude Code all day.

stories.title: Claudette: Make Claude stop talking like a BuzzFeed article
stories.blurb: A prompt-engineering library that strips Claude's output of the filler phrases, excessive bullet points, and hollow enthusiasm that plague its default responses. If you've ever groaned at "Certainly! Here's a comprehensive overview," this is for you. Drop it into your Claude Code system prompt today.

stories.title: AI boosted homework scores, then exam scores dropped: study
stories.blurb: The Economist's data team found a clear pattern: AI assistance inflated short-term performance while tanking retention and exam results. The implications stretch well beyond education — this is the clearest empirical evidence yet for the cognitive offloading trap that developers using AI coding assistants should think hard about.

stories.title: Building an (almost) fully self-hosted, sandboxed, agentic software factory
stories.blurb: A detailed walkthrough of wiring together local LLMs, sandboxed execution environments, and orchestration layers into a self-hosted coding agent pipeline. If you're experimenting beyond Claude Code or want offline agentic workflows, this is the most actionable architecture post of the week.

stories.title: iAmCorey/Wake: Every coding-agent session on your Mac in one place — browse, search, resume. Rust + GPUI.
stories.blurb: Wake is a native macOS app (built in Rust with Zed's GPUI framework) that indexes all your coding-agent sessions — Claude Code, Cursor, Aider — and lets you browse, search, and resume them in one place. If you run multiple agents across projects, this fills an obvious gap. Very new, worth watching.

stories.title: Casey Newton si è costruito una wiki personale con gli LLM, su idea di Karpathy
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: N8N, #AI_and_Tech, AI&TECH, TW2026-34, BF
stories.blurb: Casey Newton (Platformer) details his Karpathy-inspired LLM-powered personal wiki built inside Obsidian — it auto-updates pages, timelines, and concept nodes from notes, archives, and sources. This is exactly the kind of AI-augmented PKM workflow that Obsidian users have been theorising about. The Italian summary is a bonus; the English source link is the payload.

stories.title: Claude Academy · Learn to work and build with Claude
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: ai, learning, resources
stories.blurb: Anthropic's official learning hub for Claude just launched, covering everything from basic prompting to rolling out Claude across a team. If you're onboarding colleagues onto Claude Code or building internal tooling, the structured resources here beat scattered blog posts. Bookmark this one.

stories.title: fx: Tiny, open, embeddable, native coding agent
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: linux, windows, shell, programming, ai, llm, ai-assisted, opensource, simplicity, minimalism
stories.blurb: Vercel Labs' fx is a minimal, embeddable coding agent you can drop into any project or CI pipeline — think Claude Code but stripped to its essential loop and open-sourced. The emphasis on minimalism and embeddability makes it interesting for custom agentic workflows that don't want the full IDE integration overhead.

stories.title: A Practical Guide to Reducing Token Spend
stories.blurb: Concrete, actionable techniques for cutting LLM API costs without sacrificing output quality — prompt compression, caching strategies, model routing, and context window hygiene. If you're building production AI workflows, your API bill will thank you for reading this.

stories.title: Build models. Understand AI.
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: llms, editors, apps, macos, tohomebrew, tolearn, totry, onlinelearning, via:twitter
stories.blurb: Language Model Builder is a free Mac app that guides you through training a small language model from scratch — tokenizer, data selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, and chat. It's the most hands-on way to actually understand what Claude is doing under the hood, and it runs entirely local.

stories.title: Introducing Dashboard Touch, a build-your-own version of Touch ID - Anil Dash
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: hardware, mac, macos, apple, software
stories.blurb: Anil Dash documents his DIY Touch ID-style fingerprint authentication widget for macOS, with the full source on GitHub. It's a clever hack for those who want biometric convenience on machines or setups that Apple doesn't officially support. The companion repo (anildash/dashtouch) has all the code.

stories.title: AprilNEA/OpenLogi: ⚡️A native, local-first alternative to Logitech Options+, written in Rust 🦀 — remap buttons, DPI, and SmartShift over HID++. No account, no telemetry.
stories.blurb: If you use a Logitech mouse and loathe the bloated, cloud-connected Options+ software, OpenLogi is the answer: full button remapping, DPI, and SmartShift control over HID++ with zero telemetry and plain TOML config. Native, open-source, and works on macOS. Install this today.

stories.title: Metalterm — the terminal your GPU draws
stories.blurb: Metalterm is a new macOS terminal emulator that renders entirely via Apple's Metal GPU API, targeting buttery-smooth scrolling and sub-frame latency that CPU-based renderers can't match. For devs spending hours in the terminal, this could be the Ghostty-competitor worth watching. Very early but the tech is sound.

stories.title: Git at any scale
stories.blurb: Cursor's engineering blog digs into the architectural challenges of making Git workflows scale across massive codebases and multi-agent environments — directly relevant as AI coding tools multiply the rate of commits and merges. Practical insights on partial clones, sparse checkouts, and commit throughput that apply well beyond Cursor itself.
